title: Luxo Jr., Pixar's lamp
hook: Pixar's hopping lamp starred in the first 3D computer-animated film up for an Oscar.
peek: In 1986 John Lasseter made a two-minute film about a big desk lamp and a small one playing with a ball. It became the first 3D computer-animated film nominated for an Academy Award, and the little lamp still hops across Pixar's logo.
lede: In 1986 the young company Pixar showed a two-minute film called Luxo Jr. at SIGGRAPH, a computer graphics conference. It starred two desk lamps, a parent and a child, and a rubber ball. There was no dialogue, yet audiences read real feelings into the lamps. The next year it became the first 3D computer-animated film nominated for an Oscar.

bullets.text: Director John Lasseter modelled the characters on the Luxo lamp on his own desk. He imagined what a baby lamp would look like, keeping the bulb size the same but shrinking the other parts, much as a baby has a large head.

Lasseter had first planned a simple motion study. He has said that the Belgian animator Raoul Servais urged him to give even a short film a beginning, middle and end, so the little lamp gets a ball, pops it, and comes back with a bigger one.
Luxo Jr. was nominated for Best Animated Short Film in 1987. It did not win, but it showed that computer animation could carry character and comedy, not only technical demonstrations.
The little lamp became Pixar's mascot. Before its films, Luxo Jr. hops onto the I in the Pixar name and squashes it flat, then turns to look at the audience.
